topic.subject: science
topic.title: Light: mirrors and lenses
topic.scope: plane mirror image, concave and convex mirrors and lenses, real and virtual images, dispersion of white light

nodes.name: Real images can be on screens
Virtual images cannot be on screens

misconceptions.statement: Light can bend around corners like sound does.
misconceptions.why: Students observe light filling a room even if the source is hidden.
misconceptions.fix: Light travels only in straight lines; it fills a room by reflecting off multiple surfaces.

probe.question: If you place a cardboard with a tiny hole between a candle and your eye, but move the hole slightly to the left, can you still see the flame?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the light will curve through the hole to reach my eye.

misconceptions.root_belief: light behaves like a fluid or gas

misconceptions.statement: The image in a plane mirror is located on the surface of the glass.
misconceptions.why: The mirror surface is the physical boundary where the reflection occurs.
misconceptions.fix: The image is formed behind the mirror at the same distance as the object is in front.

probe.question: If you stand 2 meters away from a mirror, where is your image located?
probe.wrong_answer: On the glass surface of the mirror.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you see is where it is

misconceptions.statement: Lateral inversion means the image is upside down.
misconceptions.why: Confusion between the terms 'inversion' and 'lateral inversion'.
misconceptions.fix: Lateral inversion means the left side of the object appears as the right side of the image, but it remains upright.

probe.question: When you raise your right hand in front of a plane mirror, what does your image do?
probe.wrong_answer: It raises its hand but appears upside down.

misconceptions.root_belief: a word means its everyday meaning

misconceptions.statement: Virtual images are not real and cannot be seen by the human eye.
misconceptions.why: The word 'virtual' is interpreted as 'imaginary' or 'non-existent' in everyday language.
misconceptions.fix: Virtual images are real optical phenomena that we can see, but they cannot be projected onto a screen.

probe.question: Can you see the image formed by a plane mirror if you don't have a screen?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because virtual images aren't actually there to be seen.

misconceptions.statement: A concave mirror always makes things look bigger.
misconceptions.why: Students often only use concave mirrors (like makeup mirrors) at very close distances.
misconceptions.fix: Concave mirrors can form smaller, same-sized, or larger images depending on the object's distance.

probe.question: What happens to the size of the image in a concave mirror as you move very far away from it?
probe.wrong_answer: It stays larger than the object.

misconceptions.root_belief: one observation applies to all cases

misconceptions.statement: A prism adds colors to white light.
misconceptions.why: The prism is seen as the 'source' of the colors because white light looks 'pure'.
misconceptions.fix: White light already contains all seven colors; the prism only separates them.

probe.question: Where do the colors of a rainbow come from when light passes through a prism?
probe.wrong_answer: The glass of the prism changes the light into different colors.

misconceptions.statement: If you walk away from a plane mirror, your image gets smaller.
misconceptions.why: Objects further away look smaller due to perspective, so students assume the image itself shrinks.
misconceptions.fix: The size of the image in a plane mirror remains exactly the same as the object, regardless of distance.

probe.question: If you move 5 meters back from a mirror, does the actual height of your image change?

misconceptions.root_belief: appearance is the same as physical reality

misconceptions.statement: A real image can only exist if there is a screen to catch it.
misconceptions.why: The definition 'can be obtained on a screen' is interpreted as 'requires a screen to form'.
misconceptions.fix: A real image forms in space where light rays actually meet; a screen just allows us to see it from all angles.

probe.question: If a concave mirror forms a real image but you remove the screen, does the image still exist in space?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the image disappears because there is no screen.

misconceptions.statement: All lenses are used to magnify objects.
misconceptions.why: Common experience with 'magnifying glasses' (convex lenses) is generalized to all lenses.
misconceptions.fix: Lenses can either converge or diverge light; concave lenses always make objects look smaller.

probe.question: Does a concave lens make a distant building look larger or smaller?
probe.wrong_answer: Larger, because that is what lenses do.

misconceptions.root_belief: all members of a category are identical

misconceptions.statement: We see objects because our eyes send out rays to them.
misconceptions.why: The active feeling of 'looking' at something suggests the eye is the source of the action.
misconceptions.fix: We see objects only when light from a source reflects off them and enters our eyes.

probe.question: How do you see a book in a dark room when you turn on a torch?
probe.wrong_answer: My eyes send light to the book so I can see it.

misconceptions.root_belief: perception is an active outward process

misconceptions.statement: Convex mirrors are used in cars because they make images larger.
misconceptions.why: Students assume 'better' mirrors must magnify things.
misconceptions.fix: Convex mirrors are used because they provide a wider field of view, even though images appear smaller.

probe.question: Why does a car's side mirror say 'Objects in mirror are closer than they appear'?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the mirror magnifies them to look bigger.

misconceptions.statement: Newton's disc turns white because the colors hide behind each other.
misconceptions.why: Difficulty understanding the persistence of vision and additive color mixing.
misconceptions.fix: The colors blur together in our brain so quickly that we perceive the mixture as white.

probe.question: Why does the seven-colored disc look white when rotated fast?
probe.wrong_answer: The colors move so fast they cover each other up.

misconceptions.root_belief: physical objects must occupy separate spaces
